## Learning Objectives

1.  Manipulating raster data with `rasterio`.

2.  Manipulating vector data with `geopandas`.

3.  Use `true color imagery` to understand Los Angeles landscape.

4.  Use `false color imagery` to highlight the burn markings from the 2025 Palisades and Eaton wildfires.

## Introductions

### Data sets

1.  Landsat 8 satellite recorded a collection of bands (red, green, blue, near-infrared and shortwave infrared) from the Landsat Collection 2 Level-2 atmospherically corrected surface reflectance data. Data was obtained from \[Microsoft Planetary Computer data catalogue\](<https://planetarycomputer.microsoft.com/dataset/landsat-c2-l2>).

2.  Geometries of the Eaton and Palisades fire perimeters from \[County of Los Angele's ArcGIS page\](<https://egis-lacounty.hub.arcgis.com/maps/ad51845ea5fb4eb483bc2a7c38b2370c/about>).

## Inital Steps 

First thing we must do is load all necessary libraries! 


The important libraries are the `geopandas` and `xarrary`. The `geopandas` package is useful when dealing with vector data. The fire perimeters are polygons (which is a type of vector data). Therefore, we will be using `geopandas` for the borders. Whereas, the `xarrary` package is useful when working with raster data, such as the landsat data set.
